protocols.Rehab/Low Back Pain:
# Low Back Pain — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Non-specific mechanical low back pain, muscle strain, disc irritation (no neurological signs)*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- Pain in **lower back region**, worse with certain positions or movements, better with others
- No specific injury remembered (or minor, non-traumatic onset)
- Stiffness that improves with movement and worsens with prolonged sitting
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Loss of bladder/bowel control + numbness in saddle area (cauda equina — **emergency**), bilateral leg weakness or numbness, fever + chills + back pain, unexplained weight loss, history of cancer + new back pain, night pain not relieved by changing position, morning stiffness >45 minutes (inflammatory)
- **Tissue healing tier:** Depends on cause (muscle strain: Tier 2; disc involvement: Tier 3) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Spine (cartilaginous symphyses, limited ROM) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-3)

- **Stay active within pain limits.** Bed rest is NOT recommended — it worsens outcomes. **Source: E3 Rehab, Cochrane review**
- **Reduce aggravating positions:** Prolonged sitting (>30 min), heavy lifting with poor mechanics, end-range flexion (forward bending)
- **Pain management:** Heat (not ice) for muscle stiffness. Short-term NSAIDs if needed (but see PEACE & LOVE — limit use). **Source: BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine 2025** — NSAIDs effective for acute LBP
- **Movement snacks:** Cat-cow, gentle walking, or any pain-free movement every hour. "Something is always better than nothing." **Source: E3 Rehab**

## Rehab Phase (Week 1-12+)

### Stage 1: Movement Exploration (Week 1-2)
- **Cat-cow** — 10 slow reps, focus on segmental movement
- **Supine knee rocks** (lying on back, knees bent, rock side to side) — 10 each side
- **Standing side bends** — 10 each side
- **Walking** 5-15 min/day
- **Goal:** Find which movements REDUCE pain vs INCREASE pain. There is no single "best exercise" — experiment. **Source: E3 Rehab**

### Stage 2: Trunk + Hip Strengthening (Week 2-6)
- **Dead bug** (lying on back, core engaged, opposite arm/leg lower) — 3×8 each side
- **Bird dog** (on all fours, extend opposite arm + leg, keep spine neutral) — 3×8 each side
- **Side plank** (from knees if needed) — 3×20s hold
- **Glute bridge** — 3×12
- **Frequency:** 4-5×/week
- **Pain rule:** <3/10 during, must settle within 1 hour

### Stage 3: Full Capacity (Week 6-12)
- **Squat** (bodyweight, then loaded) — 3×10
- **Deadlift** (trap bar or conventional, start light, perfect technique) **Source: E3 Rehab** — nothing is inherently off limits
- **Lunges** — 3×8 each leg
- **Carries** (suitcase, farmer's) — 3×30s each
- **Key insight:** Exercise, regardless of type, offers moderate clinical benefit for cLBP. The best exercise is one you can do consistently. **Source: BACPAC evidence review**

## Return to Training

- **Criteria:** Pain <3/10 during daily activities, able to sit 30+ min without worsening, able to walk 30 min pain-free
- **Reintroduction:**
  1. Bodyweight compound lifts (squat, hinge) with no load
  2. Add load progressively (10% per week), guided by next-day response
  3. Avoid training to failure on deadlift/squat for first 4 weeks back
- **Expectation:** It's normal for symptoms to fluctuate day-to-day. Focus on function trend, not daily pain levels. **Source: E3 Rehab**

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Heavy conventional deadlift | Trap bar deadlift, RDL | Reduces spinal shear, easier to keep neutral |
| Standing OHP (loaded) | Seated DB press, landmine press | Standing requires trunk bracing under load |
| Barbell back squat (heavy) | Goblet squat, front squat, belt squat | Less spinal compression |
| Sit-ups/crunches | Dead bug, plank, bird dog | Repeated flexion = disc pressure |
| Kettlebell swings (if painful) | Hip thrusts, glute bridges | Ballistic loading may flare symptoms |

## Prehab / Prevention

- "Movement snacks" every 2 hours during work (2-min walk, cat-cows, side bends)
- Maintain general physical activity — 30 min walking daily
- Strength training 3×/week (doesn't need to be spine-specific, just regular)
- **Sleep + stress** are as important as any exercise for LBP management
- **Early warning signs:** Stiffness returning after period of no pain → increase movement frequency. Sharp pain with a specific movement → avoid that movement for 2 weeks, then test again

---

### Video Resources

- **Squat University — How to Fix Low Back Pain (McGill Method / Big 3):** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Search "Squat University low back pain" for multiple videos covering McGill Big 3, hip hinge, and assessment
- **E3 Rehab — Low Back Pain | Lumbar Spine Rehab (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://www.youtube.com/@E3Rehab — Evidence-based guide covering directional preference, core stabilization, and return to lifting
- **E3 Rehab — The McGill Big 3 (How to Set Up and Progress):** https://www.youtube.com/@E3Rehab — Specific video on curl-up, side plank, bird dog progression
- **Squat University — 3 Best Exercises for Low Back Pain:** https://youtu.be/3pXMsvzH1Js — Exercise demo with movement correction cues

**Sources:** E3 Rehab (Low Back Pain Rehab, Low Back Resilience), BACPAC evidence review (2022), Cochrane review on exercise for cLBP (2025 update), VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for LBP

*Links to: [[04_PROTOCOLS/Injury Management Protocol.md\|Injury Management Protocol]], [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery]]*
protocols.Rehab/Patellofemoral Pain:
# Patellofemoral Pain — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Runner's knee, anterior knee pain, chondromalacia patella*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- Pain **behind or around the kneecap** with squatting, stairs, running, or prolonged sitting (movie-goer's sign)
- Gradual onset, no specific injury
- Pain may be felt in both knees
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Acute knee swelling within 2 hours (possible ligament/meniscus), locking/catching/giving way, inability to bear weight, fever + redness
- **Tissue healing tier:** Tier 3 (cartilage, no regeneration) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Knee (modified hinge) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-7)

- **Reduce aggravating loads:** Deep squats (limit to 45°), running (switch to cycling or swimming), prolonged sitting with bent knee
- **Pain management:** Ice 15 min after activity. Paracetamol if needed
- **What to continue:** Upper body training, core, hip-dominant lower body (hip thrusts, deadlifts if pain-free)
- **Isometric quad:** Wall sits at pain-free angle — hold 30s, 3-5 sets. **Source: E3 Rehab tendinopathy principles, Patelofemoral CPG (APTA 2019)**

## Rehab Phase (Week 2-8)

### Stage 1: Hip + Quad Activation (Week 2-3)
- **Clamshells** — 3×15 each side (targets glute med, key for PFPS)
- **Side-lying leg raises** — 3×15
- **Straight leg raise** (quad set first, hold 5s) — 3×10
- **Short arc quads** (small pillow under knee, lift heel) — 3×15
- **Hip bridge** — 3×12
- **Frequency:** Daily. **Source: APTA CPG** — primary treatment is targeted posterior hip + quad exercise

### Stage 2: Double Leg Loading (Week 3-5)
- **Wall sits** at 45° knee bend — 3×30-60s hold
- **Step-ups** (low step, controlled descent) — 3×10
- **Squat to chair** (partial ROM pain-free) — 3×12
- **Lateral band walks** — 3×10 steps each direction
- **Pain rule:** <3/10 during, must settle within 1 hour

### Stage 3: Single Leg + Sport-Specific (Week 5-8)
- **Bulgarian split squat** (limited ROM, front-foot elevated) — 3×8
- **Single-leg squat** to 45° — 3×8
- **Step-downs** (1-2 inch step, controlled) — 3×10
- **Pain rule:** May have mild discomfort but should NOT increase day-to-day

## Return to Running

- **Criteria:**
  - Pain-free during daily activities (stairs, sitting, squatting)
  - Single-leg squat to 60° without pain
  - Step-down test: 30 reps without pain
- **Graduated return:**
  - Week 1: Walk-run 1:3 ratio (1 min run, 3 min walk) 2×/week
  - Week 2: Walk-run 2:2 ratio, 3×/week
  - Week 3: Run 20 min continuous, flat surface, 3×/week
  - Week 4: Run 30 min, introduce gentle hills
  - **If pain returns:** Drop back one stage. Do not push through. **Source: E3 Rehab / Exakt Health run-return principles**

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Deep squats (<90°) | Half squats (to 45-60°), box squats | Increases PF joint compression |
| Leg extensions (full ROM) | Short arc extensions (last 30° only) | Opens PF compression angle |
| Running downhill | Flat running, uphill walking | Eccentric load increases pain |
| Leg press (deep) | Leg press (limited to 90°) | Decreases PF stress |
| Lunges (full stride) | Reverse lunges (limited ROM) | Better control, less PF stress |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Hip glute work (clamshells, band walks) 2×/week — glute med weakness is the #1 risk factor
- VMO quad work (terminal knee extension) 2×/week
- Proper footwear: replace running shoes every 300-500 miles
- **Early warning signs:** Dull ache after running → reduce mileage 20%. Pain with prolonged sitting → take standing breaks every 30 min

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome | Runner's Knee (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://youtu.be/K3HxB6rAeDo — Covers anatomy, causes, 4-stage loading progression, taping
- **Squat University — How to Fix Runner's Knee:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment and exercise corrections for patellofemoral pain
- **E3 Rehab — Hip vs Knee vs Ankle: What to Train for Knee Pain:** https://www.youtube.com/@E3Rehab — Kinetic chain approach to knee rehab (search "E3 Rehab knee pain")
- **[P]rehab — Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome Rehab:** https://www.youtube.com/@PrehabGuys — Exercise demos and progression guidelines

**Sources:** APTA Clinical Practice Guideline for Patellofemoral Pain (Willy et al, 2019), E3 Rehab knee program principles, BMJ Best Practice Guide for PFP (2024), IQWiG/NIH conservative management

protocols.Rehab/Plantar Fasciitis:
# Plantar Fasciitis — Self-Managed Rehab

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- **Sharp heel pain** with first steps in the morning or after prolonged sitting
- Pain at the **bottom of heel** or along the arch
- Dull ache after prolonged standing/walking
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Numbness/tingling in foot (tarsal tunnel), redness + swelling + fever (infection), acute tearing sensation (possible plantar fascia rupture), bilateral heel pain + morning stiffness >45 min (inflammatory arthritis)
- **Tissue healing tier:** Tier 3 (fascia/tendon, poorly vascularized) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Foot/ankle (hinge + gliding) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-10)

- **Relative rest:** Reduce high-impact activity (running, jumping) by 50%
- **Pain management:** Ice massage (freeze water in paper cup, roll under arch for 10 min, 2×/day)
- **Footwear:** Supportive shoes with good arch support. Avoid walking barefoot on hard surfaces. **Source: Washington U Ortho, NHS**
- **What to continue:** Upper body, cycling, swimming (pain-free)
- **Night splint** if possible — holds plantar fascia in lengthened position overnight, reduces morning pain. **Source: Mayo Clinic**

## Rehab Phase (Week 1-8+)

### Stage 1: Calf + Arch Stretching (Week 1-4)
- **Towel stretch** — sit with leg straight, towel around ball of foot, pull toward you, feel stretch in calf. Hold 45s, 3 reps, 4-6×/day. **Source: Washington U Ortho**
- **Standing calf stretch** — straight back leg, heel down, lean forward. Hold 45s, 3 reps, 4-6×/day
- **Plantar fascia stretch** — sit crossed leg, pull toes toward shin. Hold 30s, 3 reps, several ×/day
- **Ice massage stretch** — freeze water bottle, roll under foot while seated — 10 min
- **Key insight:** Calf tightness is the main driver of PF. Fix the calf, fix the PF. **Source: systematic reviews, NHS guidelines**

### Stage 2: Foot Intrinsic Strengthening (Week 3-6)
- **Towel scrunches** — sit, use toes to scrunch towel toward you — 3×15
- **Marble pickups** — use toes to pick up and move marbles — 3×10
- **Arch lifts** (short foot exercise) — stand, lift arch while keeping toes + heel on ground — 3×10, hold 5s
- **Calf raises** — 3×15 (control entire range)

### Stage 3: High-Load Strength + Return (Week 6-8+)
- **Heavy calf raises** (weighted, single leg) — 3×8-12
- **Single-leg balance** on foam pad — 3×30s
- **Progressive return to running:** Walk-jog protocol (see Achilles protocol — same principles apply)
- **High-load strength training** may speed recovery more than stretching alone. **Source: Rathleff et al 2015**

## Return to Running

- **Criteria:**
  - Morning pain <2/10
  - Pain-free during walking
  - Single-leg calf raise 20+ reps pain-free
- **Graduated:**
  1. Walk 30 min pain-free → walk-jog 3:1 × 15 min
  2. Progress to continuous jog 15 min over 2 weeks
  3. Build 10% volume per week
  4. Avoid speed work until >30 min continuous running is pain-free

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Barefoot walking on hard surfaces | Supportive shoes, OOFOS/orthotics | Hard surface = more PF stress |
| High-impact plyometrics early | Cycling, swimming, elliptical | Loading before capacity = flare |
| Running on concrete | Track, trail (soft surface) | Softer surface = less impact |
| Prolonged standing | Sit breaks, anti-fatigue mat | Continuous standing strains PF |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Calf stretching daily (2 min total, broken into sessions) — lifelong habit
- Replace shoes every 300-500 miles
- Maintain ankle and hip mobility — restrictions up-chain increase foot load
- **Early warning signs:** Morning soreness that resolves in 2-3 steps vs 10+ steps = early, respond with calf work. If first steps are genuinely painful >5 min → reduce high-impact volume 30%

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — Plantar Fasciitis | Heel Pain Rehab (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://youtu.be/5D86b45yJzU — Covers anatomy, calf contribution, isometric loading, progressive strengthening, taping
- **Squat University — How to Fix Plantar Fasciitis:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment of foot mechanics and corrective exercises
- **[P]rehab — Plantar Fasciitis Exercises & Treatment:** https://www.youtube.com/@PrehabGuys — Stretching, mobilization, and strengthening demos

**Sources:** Washington U Ortho (plantar fasciitis exercises), [P]rehab (plantar fasciitis guide), NHS clinical guidelines, Mayo Clinic treatment guide

protocols.Rehab/Shin Splints:
# Shin Splints — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Medial tibial stress syndrome (MTSS)*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- **Dull ache along the inside of the shin bone** (posteromedial tibia)
- Pain during/after running or high-impact activity
- Tenderness to touch along ≥5 cm of the medial tibial border
- Gradual onset from increased training volume/intensity
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Pain in focal spot <5 cm (possible stress fracture — drop everything and see professional), sharp/burning/radiating pain, numbness/tingling in foot, severe pain with walking (compartment syndrome evaluation needed)
- **Tissue healing tier:** Tier 2 (bone stress, weeks-months) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Ankle (hinge) + knee (modified hinge) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-14)

- **Relative rest:** Reduce impact activity to pain-free level. Cross-train (cycling, swimming, elliptical). **Source: Sanford Health MTSS guideline**
- **Distinguish from stress fracture:** If pain is at a specific point <5 cm area → assume stress fracture until proven otherwise. Get medical eval.
- **Pain management:** Ice massage along shin 15 min after activity
- **What to continue:** Upper body, cycling (pain-free), swimming
- **Foot pronation check:** If excessive pronation is present → consider supportive shoes or OTC orthotics. **Source: Sanford Health, Wilder et al**

## Rehab Phase (Week 2-12+)

### Stage 1: Calf + Foot Mobility (Week 2-4)
- **Gastrocnemius stretch** (straight leg) — 3×45s, daily
- **Soleus stretch** (bent knee) — 3×45s, daily
- **Towel stretch** — 3×45s
- **Ankle mobility** (alphabet, circles, resisted inversion/eversion with band)
- **Key insight:** Calf tightness directly increases tibial stress. Fix calf, fix shins. **Source: MTSS literature**

### Stage 2: Lower Leg Strengthening (Week 3-6)
- **Calf raises** (standing, full ROM, both legs then single) — 3×15
- **Tibialis anterior raises** (heel walking, or seated dorsiflexion with band) — 3×15
- **Tibialis posterior raises** (seated calf raise with toe pointed in, or band inversion) — 3×15. **Key muscle for MTSS** — weak posterior tibialis → increased pronation → more tibial stress
- **Intrinsic foot work** (towel scrunches, arch lifts) — 3×15
- **Frequency:** Daily

### Stage 3: Return to Impact (Week 4-12)
- **Walk progression:** Pain-free walking 30 min → brisk walking
- **Graded return to running** (see below)
- **Hip and core strengthening** (single-leg balance, bridges, planks) — kinetic chain deficits contribute to MTSS
- **Pain rule:** Soreness during warm-up that resolves → OK. Pain that persists or worsens → too much too soon.

## Return to Running

- **Criteria:**
  - Pain-free with walking for 30+ min
  - No tenderness to touch along shin
  - Single-leg calf raise 25× pain-free
- **Graduated:** Use the **Soreness Rules** framework:
  - Start at 50% of pre-injury volume
  - If soreness during warm-up resolves, stay at same level
  - If soreness persists throughout or the next day → take 1-2 days off and reduce volume
- **Progression:** Walk → walk-jog → jog → run (increase 10% per week max)
- **Type classification for rate:**
  - Type I (pain only after activity): 25% workload reduction, continue
  - Type II (pain during but not restricting): 50% workload reduction
  - Type III (pain restricting performance): Relative rest, non-impact only
  - **Source: AoA Ortho MTSS classification**

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Running on concrete | Track, trail (softer surface) | Hard surfaces = higher tibial load |
| Sudden mileage increases | 10% rule — gradual buildup | Spike in volume = #1 MTSS cause |
| Running with worn shoes | Replace every 300-500 miles | Worn shoes = increased pronation |
| Calf raises on hard floor | On padded mat or with shoes | Barefoot hard surface = more shock |
| Running on camber | Flat surface, alternate direction | Camber increases unilateral tibial load |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Calf raises + tibialis posterior raises 2×/week
- Graduated training volume (never >10% weekly increase)
- Proper footwear with adequate support
- **Early warning signs:** Dull ache along shin after running → reduce volume 20% and add lower-leg strength work for 1 week before next run

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — Shin Splints | Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome Rehab (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://youtu.be/qE-GNFlMd3E — Covers anatomy, causes, 4-stage rehab progression, footwear considerations
- **Squat University — How to Fix Shin Splints:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment of running mechanics and corrective exercises
- **[P]rehab — Shin Splints Exercises & Treatment:** https://www.youtube.com/@PrehabGuys — Exercise demos and progression guidelines

**Sources:** Sanford Health MTSS Rehab Guideline, AoA Ortho MTSS Classification, Physiotutors (interview with Tom Goom), [P]rehab running return principles

protocols.Rehab/Shoulder Impingement:
# Shoulder Impingement — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Subacromial pain syndrome, rotator cuff tendinopathy, shoulder bursitis*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- Pain on **outside/top of shoulder** with overhead reaching, lifting, or lying on that side
- Painful arc between 60-120° of abduction
- Weakness without traumatic tear (difficulty lifting arm overhead)
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Acute traumatic pop/tear + inability to lift arm (possible full-thickness rotator cuff tear), fever + redness + heat (infectious), shoulder dislocation/subluxation
- **Tissue healing tier:** Varies (tendon: Tier 3; muscle: Tier 2) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Shoulder (ball-and-socket, multi-axial) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-7)

- **Reduce aggravating load:** Avoid overhead pressing, heavy lateral raises, upright rows, dips, behind-the-neck exercises
- **Pain management:** Ice after activity (15 min). Paracetamol if needed. **Source: E3 Rehab (PT-led, avoid NSAIDs for long-term healing)**
- **What to continue:** Lower body training, core work, unilateral arm work below shoulder height (neutral grip)
- **Isometric rotator cuff:** Standing at a wall, press palm into wall at 0° abduction — hold 30s, 3 sets. IR, ER, and abduction directions. **Source: E3 Rehab frozen shoulder protocol** (isometrics for high irritability)

## Rehab Phase (Week 2-6)

- **Pain goal:** ≤3/10 during exercise, must settle within 1 hour

### Stage 1: Scapular Control (Week 2)
- Prone Y raises (thumbs up, no weight, focus on scapular retraction) — 3×15
- Prone T raises — 3×15
- Prone W raises (elbows bent, squeeze shoulder blades) — 3×15
- Wall slides (walk fingers up wall, keep shoulders down) — 3×10
- **Frequency:** Daily

### Stage 2: Rotator Cuff Loading (Week 3-4)
- Side-lying external rotation (light dumbbell, pillow between arm and body) — 3×12-15
- Prone horizontal abduction at 90° (thumb up) — 3×12
- Standing external rotation with band — 3×15
- Prone extension (palm up, lift arm back) — 3×12

### Stage 3: Progressive Overhead Loading (Week 4-6)
- Landmine press (neutral grip) — 3×10
- Dumbbell press (neutral grip, partial ROM if needed) — 3×8-10
- Cable face pulls (high priority — scapular retraction + ER) — 3×15
- Band pull-aparts — 3×15
- **Key insight from literature:** Exercise therapy is first-line and as effective as surgery for most impingement. No one "best exercise" — find what works through trial and error. **Source: E3 Rehab, Kuhn 2009 systematic review**

## Return to Training

- **Criteria:**
  - Pain-free full active ROM (especially overhead)
  - No painful arc
  - 90% strength symmetry on IR/ER compared to uninjured side
- **Reintroduction:** Start with neutral-grip pressing, avoid full-range overhead pressing for 2 more weeks. Progress: landmine → dumbbell → barbell overhead

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Barbell overhead press | Landmine press, dumbbell neutral grip | Reduces impingement risk at end range |
| Upright rows | Band pull-aparts, cable face pulls | Upright rows compress subacromial space |
| Behind-the-neck pull-downs | Front pull-downs or pull-ups | End-range IR compresses rotator cuff |
| Dips (deep) | Partial ROM dips or bench dips | Deep dips stress anterior shoulder |
| Flat barbell bench (wide grip) | Dumbbell press (neutral, narrower) | Wide grip increases shoulder stress |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Continue face pulls 2-3×/week indefinitely — single most evidence-supported prehab exercise for shoulders
- Band pull-aparts on upper body days
- Thoracic spine mobility (foam roller extension) — reduced thoracic extension → impingement risk
- **Early warning signs:** Clicking without pain = OK. Clicking + dull ache = reduce overhead volume immediately

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — Shoulder Impingement Rehab | Subacromial Pain (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://youtu.be/1Wy8jh4QQH8 — Covers anatomy, mechanism, scapular control, rotator cuff loading, 4-stage progression
- **Squat University — How to Fix Shoulder Impingement:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment of shoulder mechanics and corrective exercises
- **E3 Rehab — 15 Best Rotator Cuff Exercises:** https://www.youtube.com/@E3Rehab — Exercise library for rotator cuff strength (search "E3 Rehab rotator cuff")
- **[P]rehab — Shoulder Impingement Exercises & Treatment:** https://www.youtube.com/@PrehabGuys — Exercise demos and progression guidelines

**Sources:** E3 Rehab (Shoulder Resilience program, Rotator Cuff Tear Rehab, Truth About Impingement), Kuhn 2009 systematic review, clinical practice guidelines (exercise as first-line intervention)

*Links to: [[04_PROTOCOLS/Injury Management Protocol.md\|Injury Management Protocol]], [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 5 - Strength Maxing.md\|P5 Strength]]*
protocols.Rehab/SI Joint Dysfunction:
# SI Joint Dysfunction — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Sacroiliac joint pain, sacroiliitis (non-inflammatory), pelvic girdle pain*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- Pain **deep in the buttock, on one side** — may refer down back of leg (but NOT past the knee typically)
- Worse with **sitting on that side**, standing on one leg, or during transitional movements (standing from sitting)
- Worse during or after running (especially on uneven surfaces)
- Pain with **asymmetric loading** (lunges, single-leg work)
- Often misdiagnosed as lumbar back pain — SI joint is just lateral to the spine, around belt level
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Bilateral leg numbness, loss of bladder/bowel control (cauda equina — emergency), fever, unexplained weight loss, morning stiffness >45 min (inflammatory), positive SLR test down past knee (discogenic)
- **Tissue healing tier:** Tier 3 (ligament, poorly vascularized) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** SI joint (cartilaginous, limited ROM) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-5)

- **Reduce asymmetrical loading:** Avoid lunges, single-leg work, running on cambered surfaces
- **Pain management:** Heat on the affected side before activity. Ice after if flare
- **Sitting modification:** Use a small lumbar roll or sit on the non-painful side. Avoid sitting on thick wallets
- **What to continue:** Upper body (seated), core (symmetrical — dead bugs, planks), bilateral lower body (squats to parallel, deadlifts from floor)

## Rehab Phase (Week 1-8+)

### Stage 1: Core Stabilization + Pelvis Control (Week 1-3)
- **Dead bug** — 3×10 each side (focus on maintaining pelvis neutral)
- **Side plank** (from knees if needed) — 3×20s each side
- **Glute bridge** (bilateral, squeeze glutes first before lifting) — 3×12
- **Supine knee rolls** (lying on back, knees bent together, roll side to side, keep upper back flat) — 10 each direction
- **Single-leg balance** (barefoot, 30s, progress to eyes closed) — 3 reps each
- **Source:** Pure Physiotherapy, Good Hands PT

### Stage 2: Glute + Lateral Hip Loading (Week 3-6)
- **Clamshells** (band above knee) — 3×15 each side
- **Side-lying leg raises** — 3×15 each side
- **Lateral band walks** — 3×10 steps each direction
- **Single-leg bridge** — 3×10 each side
- **Squat** (bodyweight, focus on knee tracking, symmetrical weight distribution) — 3×10
- **Pain rule:** ≤4/10 during, no worsening next day. **Source: Pure Physiotherapy**

### Stage 3: Asymmetric Loading + Return (Week 6-8+)
- **Lunges** (reverse, short stride, controlled) — 3×8 each
- **Step-ups** (low step, controlled) — 3×10 each
- **Single-leg squat** (to 45°, controlled descent) — 3×8 each
- **Running return** (flat surface, gradual)

## Return to Training

- **Criteria:**
  - Pain-free during daily activities
  - Single-leg stance 30s without pain
  - Squat to 90° without pain
- **Reintroduction:**
  1. Bilateral work only (squat, deadlift, bridges) for 1-2 weeks
  2. Add unilateral work (lunges, step-ups) gradually
  3. Running: Start walk-jog on flat surface, avoid cambered roads
  4. Avoid explosive unilateral work (sprinting, hopping) until >4 weeks symptom-free
- **Key insight:** SI joint responds well to motor control work + glute med strength. Manual therapy alone provides temporary relief. **Source: Good Hands PT clinical data**

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Lunges (early) | Bilateral squats, bridges | Asymmetric loading may irritate SIJ |
| Single-leg deadlifts | Bilateral RDL | Heavy single-leg = asymmetric load |
| Running on camber | Flat track (alternate direction) | Camber = pelvic asymmetry |
| Sprinting | Gradual acceleration | High force = more SIJ stress |
| Heavy farmer's carries | Suitcase carries (light) or bilateral | Asymmetric loading = SIJ risk |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Glute med work (clamshells, band walks) 2×/week — lifelong for SIJ stability
- Core stabilization (dead bugs, planks) 2×/week
- Avoid prolonged sitting >45 min without standing break
- **Early warning signs:** Dull ache in one buttock after long sitting → increase standing breaks + glute activation

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — SI Joint Pain | Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction (Education | Myths | Exercises):** https://youtu.be/h7UWxp9hWpg — Covers anatomy, differentiation from lumbar pain, 4-stage rehab progression
- **Squat University — How to Fix SI Joint Pain:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment and corrective exercises for SI joint dysfunction
- **[P]rehab — Pelvic Pain Exercises:** https://www.youtube.com/@PrehabGuys — Related exercises for pelvic stability

**Sources:** Good Hands Physical Therapy (SIJ rehabilitation 8-week protocol), Pure Physiotherapy (SIJ early/advanced programs), Medtronic (SIJ strengthening), SI-BONE rehabilitation resource

*Links to: [[04_PROTOCOLS/Injury Management Protocol.md\|Injury Management Protocol]], [[04_PROTOCOLS/Rehab/Low Back Pain.md\|Low Back Pain Protocol]]*
protocols.Rehab/Wrist Overuse:
# Wrist Overuse — Self-Managed Rehab

*Also applies to: Wrist tendinitis, De Quervain's tenosynovitis (thumb side), carpal tunnel (mild), wrist strain*

---

**Evidence sources:** [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Junqueira's Basic Histology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Junqueira Ch 5,7,10]] (tissue healing hierarchy, collagen types) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Seeley's Anatomy and Physiology 2019/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Seeley Ch 8]] (joint classification, anatomy) | [[08_EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE/Books/Guyton and Hall - Textbook of Medical Physiology 14ed/03 Extracted Concepts.md\|Guyton Ch 72,85]] (metabolic adaptation, energy systems)

## When This Protocol Applies

- Pain in the **wrist** aggravated by gripping, pushing, or repetitive wrist movements
- Pain on **thumb side of wrist** that radiates up forearm (De Quervain's)
- **Mild** numbness/tingling in thumb/index fingers (mild carpal tunnel) — worse at night
- Gradual onset from increased volume (push-ups, handstands, typing, lifting)
- **Red flags → do NOT self-treat:** Severe/persistent numbness (possible nerve compression), wrist locking/catching, swelling + redness + heat, deformity, trauma with inability to move wrist
- **Tissue healing tier:** Tier 3 (tendon, poorly vascularized, months-years) — Junqueira Ch 5,7,10. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Tissue Healing Hierarchy]]
- **Joint classification:** Wrist (condylar, bi-axial) — Seeley Ch 8. See [[02_PILLARS/Pillar 4 - Recovery Maxing.md\|P4 Recovery — Joint Classification Reference]]

---

## Acute Phase (Days 1-7)

- **Reduce aggravating loads:** Push-ups (use fists or push-up bars), heavy gripping (use straps), wrist extension/flexion exercises
- **Pain management:** Ice 15 min post-activity. Paracetamol if needed
- **Splinting:** For De Quervain's — thumb spica splint. For carpal tunnel — neutral wrist splint at night only
- **What to continue:** Lower body, core, pulling exercises (if pain-free with neutral grip)

## Rehab Phase (Week 1-6+)

### Stage 1: Isometric + Range of Motion (Week 1-2)
- **Wrist extension isometric** (palm flat on table, push hand UP against immovable object, hold 30s) — 3 reps
- **Wrist flexion isometric** (palm up under table, push UP, hold 30s) — 3 reps
- **Grip isometric** (squeeze ball or putty, hold 30s at tolerable intensity) — 3 reps
- **Pain-free ROM:** Wrist circles, flexion/extension, radial/ulnar deviation — 10 each direction, 2×/day
- **Frequency:** 2×/day
- **Source:** E3 Rehab (tennis elbow principles applied to wrist)

### Stage 2: Isotonic Loading (Week 2-4)
- **Wrist curls** (light dumbbell, palm up) — 3×12-15
- **Reverse wrist curls** (light dumbbell, palm down) — 3×12-15
- **Farmer's carry** (light kettlebell, maintain neutral wrist) — 3×30s
- **Rice bucket** (digs, flicks, rotations — 30s each direction) — 3 sets
- **Frequency:** Every other day
- **Pain rule:** ≤3/10 during, must settle within 1 hour

### Stage 3: Full Capacity (Week 4-6+)
- **Pull-ups** (neutral grip, pain-free)
- **Push-ups** (on fists or bars)
- **Dumbbell bench** (neutral grip, controlled)
- **Loaded carries** (progressively heavier)

## Return to Training

- **Criteria:**
  - Pain-free during daily activities (typing, lifting objects)
  - Full pain-free ROM (flexion, extension, deviation)
  - Grip strength ≥80% of uninjured side
- **Reintroduction:**
  1. Neutral grip first (all pressing/pulling)
  2. Add pronated/supinated grip gradually
  3. Avoid end-range wrist extension under load initially

## Exercise Modifications

| Avoid | Substitute | Why |
|-------|-----------|-----|
| Push-ups on floor | Push-ups on fists, push-up bars, or dumbbells | Neutral wrist position reduces compression |
| Bench press (standard) | Dumbbell press (neutral grip) | Neutral grip = less wrist extension |
| Barbell curls | EZ bar, dumbbell, or cable | EZ bar reduces wrist strain |
| Pull-ups (pronated) | Neutral grip (parallel bars) or straps | Neutral grip = less wrist load |
| Handstands | Wrist-support surface or parallettes | Extreme wrist extension = high load |

## Prehab / Prevention

- Wrist mobility: Flexion/extension stretch 2×/day (if your goals require wrist ROM like handstands or yoga)
- Progressive loading for wrist-intensive exercises — don't jump from zero to high volume
- **Early warning signs:** Soreness the day after gym that persists >24 hours → reduce wrist-intensive volume 40%

---

### Video Resources

- **E3 Rehab — Elbow & Wrist Rehab Playlist:** https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLK514QIbc_RgR4RHzMWB5yeu5sMQu5W_d — Comprehensive collection covering wrist tendinopathy, carpal tunnel, forearm strengthening
- **E3 Rehab — Wrist Pain Rehab | Wrist Tendinopathy (Wrist Flexor, Extensor, ECU, De Quervain's):** https://www.youtube.com/@E3Rehab — Search "E3 Rehab wrist pain" for specific video on wrist overuse rehab
- **Squat University — Wrist Pain When Lifting?:** https://www.youtube.com/@SquatUniversity — Assessment of lifting mechanics and corrective exercises for wrist pain

**Sources:** E3 Rehab (elbow/wrist principles), NHS guidelines for wrist pain, Cleveland Clinic (carpal tunnel)

# Injury-Training Compatibility Matrix

For each injury, classifies all major training movements as **Safe (Green)**, **Modified (Yellow — with plane/ROM/load change)**, or **Contraindicated (Red)**. This extends the Default Exercise Pool injury overrides by providing a full-body training classification rather than site-specific replacements.

## How to Use

1. Identify the active injury
2. Find the corresponding matrix row
3. Train all **Green** exercises normally
4. Apply the noted modification for **Yellow** exercises
5. Remove or fully substitute **Red** exercises
6. Apply the Kinetic Chain Override System for exercises in adjacent kinetic links

---

## Upper Body Injuries

### Shoulder Impingement / Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chest** | DB Fly (neutral), Machine Press, Cable Crossover | Incline DB Press (45° max, neutral grip), Flat DB Press (stop 2" above chest) | Barbell Bench Press (wide grip), Dips (deep), Decline Press |
| **Back** | Lat Pulldown (neutral grip), Seated Row, Chest-Supported Row, Face Pull (low pulley) | Pull-Up (use assisted if needed), T-Bar Row | Behind-the-Neck Pulldown, Upright Row, Heavy Bent-Over Row |
| **Shoulders** | Lateral Raise (thumb-up, below 90°), Prone Y raise, Band pull-apart | DB OHP (neutral grip, partial ROM to ear level), Front Raise (thumb-up) | Barbell OHP, Behind-the-Neck Press, Upright Row, Arnold Press |
| **Arms** | All biceps curls, Triceps push-down (rope) | Overhead triceps extension (keep elbow in line) | French press (skull crusher), Close-grip bench press (if painful at bottom) |
| **Legs / Core** | All lower body exercises | — | — |
| **Other** | Walking, cycling, running | — | Overhead carries, handstands, heavy farmer's carries |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Reduce ROM to pain-free arc. Use neutral grip where possible. Limit load to <70% 1RM for overhead work. Prioritize scapular control before increasing load.

---

### Elbow Tendinopathy (Lateral/Medial)

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chest** | Machine Press, DB Press (neutral grip), Push-Up (on fists or handles) | Barbell Bench (narrow grip, stop 2" above chest) | Dips, Close-grip bench (full ROM) |
| **Back** | Lat Pulldown (use straps), Seated Row (use straps), Chest-Supported Row | Pull-Up (use straps, neutral grip), T-Bar Row (straps) | Bent-Over Row (no straps), Dead-hang pull-ups |
| **Shoulders** | DB OHP (neutral), Lateral Raise, Rear Delt Fly | Barbell OHP (use straps or wrist wrap) | — |
| **Arms** | Preacher Curl (EZ bar), Hammer Curl, Reverse Curl | Bayjan Curl (light, use straps) | Heavy barbell curl, Heavy triceps push-down (rope OK), French press |
| **Legs** | All lower body | — | — |
| **Grip-dependent** | Farmer's carry (use straps or hooks), Deadlift (use straps or hook grip) | RDL (use straps) | Heavy gripping without assistance, pull-ups without straps |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Use lifting straps or hooks for ALL pulling exercises. Reduce grip-intensive work. Wrist extension/flexion exercises become primary rehab.

---

### Wrist Overuse / Tendinitis

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chest** | Machine Press, Push-Up (on parallettes/fists), DB Bench (neutral) | DB Bench (supinated or neutral), Push-Up (on floor with neutral wrist) | Barbell Bench (full grip), Dips, Push-Up (hands flat) |
| **Back** | Lat Pulldown (use straps), Seated Row (use straps), Chest-Supported Row | Pull-Up (use straps) | Bent-Over Row (conventional grip), Dead-hang |
| **Shoulders** | DB OHP, Lateral Raise, Rear Delt (DB) | — | Barbell OHP, Upright Row |
| **Arms** | Hammer Curl, Reverse Curl (EZ bar) | Preacher Curl (EZ bar, light), Triceps Push-Down (rope, light) | Heavy barbell curl, Heavy triceps extension, Wrist curls |
| **Legs** | All lower body | — | — |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Use straps or hooks for any pulling. Consider wrist wraps for pushing. Avoid full wrist extension under load.

---

## Lower Body Injuries

### Patellofemoral Pain / Runner's Knee

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Quads / Squat** | Leg Press (high reps, 60° ROM), Hack Squat (to 90°), Goblet Squat (partial), Spanish Squat (45° wall sit) | Back Squat (to 60°, slow descent), Front Squat (to 60°) | Full-depth Back Squat, Bulgarian Split Squat (deep), Sissy Squat, Heavy Leg Extension (0-30°) |
| **Hinge** | RDL, Hip Thrust, 45° Hyperextension | Deadlift (trap bar, controlled), Good Morning (light) | — |
| **Single Leg** | Step-Up (shallow, 6"), Reverse Lunge (short stride) | Lunge (forward, limited ROM), Bulgarian Split Squat (to 60°, torso upright) | Deep Lunge, Step-Down (full ROM) |
| **Legs (other)** | Leg Curl, Standing Calf Raise, Adduction/Abduction | — | — |
| **Cardio** | Cycling (high cadence, low resistance), Swimming, Elliptical (low resistance) | Running (flat, alternate direction, reduce mileage 30%) | Downhill running, Running on camber, Jumping rope on concrete, Sprinting |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Pain during exercise should not exceed 3/10. If pain is >3/10, reduce ROM further. Avoid end-range knee flexion under load. Prioritize hip strengthening (abductors, glutes) alongside quad work.

### IT Band Syndrome

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Squat** | Back Squat (to 90°), Goblet Squat (to 90°), Hack Squat | Front Squat (limited to 60° if lateral knee pain) | Deep Squat (<90°), Bulgarian Split Squat |
| **Hinge** | RDL, Hip Thrust, 45° Hyperextension | Deadlift (trap bar, to knee level), Good Morning | — |
| **Single Leg** | Step-Up (shallow), Reverse Lunge (short stride) | Lunge (forward), Bulgarian Split Squat (limited ROM to 60°) | Side lunge |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical, Flat running (alternate direction) | — | Downhill running, Running on cambered surfaces, Sprinting |
| **Hip/Glute** | Clamshell, Side-lying leg raise, Lateral band walk, Hip thrust (bilateral) | Single-leg hip thrust, Step-down (shallow) | — |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Pain on lateral knee during squatting → reduce depth. Pain during running → reduce mileage, switch to flat even surfaces, alternate direction every 400m.

### Hamstring Strain / Proximal Hamstring Tendinopathy

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hinge** | RDL (partial ROM, bent knee), Hip Thrust, 45° Hyperextension (to parallel) | Deadlift (trap bar, stop above knee), Good Morning (light, 30° torso) | Conventional Deadlift (full ROM), Stiff-Leg Deadlift, Good Morning (full ROM) |
| **Squat** | All squat variations (hamstring is synergist, usually tolerated) | Deep Back Squat (if provocation at bottom) | — |
| **Legs (other)** | Leg Curl (seated, lighter), Leg Extension, Standing Calf Raise | Leg Curl (lying, eccentric phase slow) | Heavy Nordic Curl (full eccentric), Straight-leg bridge |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Walking | Flat running (gradual acceleration, avoid max speed) | Sprinting, Hill sprints, Hurdle drills |
| **Stretching** | — | Gentle hamstring flossing (nerve gliding) | Toe-touch stretching, deep forward folds, Pigeon pose |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Avoid end-range hamstring lengthening under load. Nordic curls should start from partial ROM (only lower 30°). Return to sprinting is the LAST phase — do not rush.

### Calf Strain / Soleus Strain

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calves** | Seated Calf Raise, Pogo hops (stiff), Double-leg standing calf raise (partial) | Single-leg calf raise (to pain threshold, use eccentric control) | Heavy single-leg calf raise (full ROM on step), Sprinting, Jumping rope |
| **Squat** | Back Squat, Front Squat, Goblet Squat | — | — |
| **Hinge** | RDL, Deadlift, Hip Thrust | — | — |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical | Walking (gait retraining), Flat running (gradual, soft surface) | Hill running, Sprinting, Jumping, Running on hard surfaces |
| **Other** | — | — | Heavy plyometrics, Drop jumps |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Pain at origin (medial gastroc) vs. muscle belly vs. soleus dictates modification. Soleus strain → seated calf raises preferred. Gastroc strain → straight-leg loading limited.

### Achilles Tendinopathy

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calves** | Isometric calf holds (45s, heavy), Seated calf raise, Double-leg heel raise | Single-leg calf raise (pain ≤3/10 during), Eccentric heel drop (slow) | Heavy single-leg calf raise on step (full ROM), Ballistic stretching, Bouncing calf stretch |
| **Squat** | All squat variations | — | — |
| **Hinge** | All hinge variations | — | — |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical, Water running | Flat running (reduce mileage 30-50%, every other day) | Hill running, Sprinting, Running on uneven terrain, Jumping rope |
| **Plyometrics** | — | Pogo hops (stiff, low amplitude) | Drop jumps, Box jumps, Depth jumps |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Tendinopathy responds to LOAD, not rest. Isometrics for pain relief (5x45s holds). Progress through isometric → isotonic → plyometric over 12+ weeks. Pain 24h post-exercise should not exceed pre-exercise baseline.

### Plantar Fasciitis / Plantar Heel Pain

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calves/Feet** | Plantar fascia massage (frozen bottle), Toe curls, Towel scrunches, Calf stretch (gastroc + soleus) | Single-leg calf raise (on flat surface, not step), Seated calf raise | Heavy single-leg calf raise on step, Ballistic calf stretching |
| **Squat** | All squat variations (heeled squat reduces PF tension) | — | — |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical, Water running | Walking (supportive shoes, reduce steps if painful), Flat running (reduce mileage 30%) | Barefoot running, Running on concrete, Jumping rope on hard surfaces |
| **Other** | — | — | Heavy plyometrics on hard surfaces, Prolonged standing |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Morning pain is the key outcome measure. If AM first-step pain decreases week-over-week, rehab is working. Supportive shoes with arch support reduce symptoms acutely. Night splint for persistent morning pain.

### Shin Splints (Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome)

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calves/Shins** | Toe raises (dorsiflexion strengthening), Heel walks, Calf stretch (gastroc + soleus) | Seated calf raise, Standing calf raise (double leg, partial) | Running-based plyometrics, Jumping |
| **Squat** | All squat variations | — | — |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical, Water running | Walking (pain-free only), Flat running (every 3rd day, soft surface, reduce mileage 50%) | Running on hard surfaces, Sprinting, Hill running, Running on consecutive days |
| **Bone loading** | — | Gradual loading only: start with 25% of pre-injury mileage, increase 10% per week | Impact loading > maintenance level (walking) until pain-free with daily activities |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Must distinguish from stress fracture (focal pain <5cm → suspect stress fracture → medical referral). MTSS = diffuse pain >5cm along posterior medial tibia.

### Groin Strain / Adductor-Related Pain

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Adductors** | Supine adductor squeeze (isometric, 45s hold), Copenhagen plank (isometric, partial ROM) | Side-lying adduction (light), Standing adduction (cable, light, slow) | Wide-stance squat, Heavy side lunge, Kicking, High-speed side-to-side drills |
| **Squat** | Narrow-stance squat, Front Squat, Goblet Squat | Back Squat (moderate stance, slow descent) | Wide-stance back squat, Sumo deadlift |
| **Single Leg** | Lunges (short stride, forward), Step-up (shallow), Bulgarian Split Squat (narrow stance) | Reverse lunge, Lateral lunge (short ROM) | Heavy lateral lunge (full ROM), Side planche, Wide single-leg work |
| **Cardio** | Cycling, Swimming, Elliptical | Straight-line running (gradual build), Flat running (avoid cutting) | Sprinting, Cutting, Side shuffling, Kicking sports |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Adductor loading is the treatment — but must be dosed correctly. Pain >3/10 during exercise → regress to isometric only. Copenhagen planks are the gold standard exercise.

### Hip Flexor Strain / Iliopsoas-Related Pain

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hip Flexors** | Seated leg raise (isometric, 45s), Supine marching (pain-free ROM) | Standing hip flexion (band, light, controlled), Half-kneeling stretch (gentle) | Heavy hanging leg raises, Psoas marching with weight, Sprinting, High knee running drills |
| **Squat** | Back Squat, Front Squat, Goblet Squat (pain-free depth) | Deep Squat (if hip flexor pain at bottom) | — |
| **Core** | Dead bug, Plank, Side plank, Pallof press | Hanging knee raise (partial, to parallel) | Hanging leg raise (full range), Hanging windshield wiper, Toes-to-bar |
| **Cardio** | Cycling (seat high, low resistance), Swimming | Walking (focus on hip extension), Flat running (reduce high-knee phases) | Hill running (up), Sprinting, High-knee drills, Running with exaggerated knee drive |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Sit-to-stand test is diagnostic. If painful to rise from seated → begin with isometrics in supine. Progress to standing before adding dynamic movement.

### SI Joint Dysfunction / Pelvic Girdle Pain

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Squat** | Goblet Squat (narrow stance), Front Squat | Back Squat (narrow stance, to 90°, belt optional for feedback) | Wide-stance squat, Asymmetrical squat loading (holding DB on one side) |
| **Hinge** | RDL (light, narrow stance), Hip Thrust (bilateral), 45° Hyperextension (to parallel) | Deadlift (trap bar, light, narrow stance) | Single-leg RDL, Heavy conventional deadlift, Good Morning (full ROM) |
| **Single Leg** | Step-Up (shallow, 6"), Reverse Lunge (short stride, controlled) | Lunge (forward, short stride) | Heavy lunge (deep), Bulgarian Split Squat (deep), Single-leg deadlift (heavy) |
| **Carrying** | Suitcase carry (light, <25% BW), Farmer's carry (bilateral, light) | Farmer's carry (heavy, keep core braced), Suitcase carry (moderate, 25-40% BW) | Heavy unilateral carries (>50% BW), Single-arm overhead carry |
| **Core** | Dead bug, Side plank, Bird dog, Pallof press | — | Heavy Russian twist, Full sit-up, Heavy side bend |
| **Cardio** | Walking (flat), Cycling, Elliptical | Flat running (even surfaces, reduce stride length) | Running on camber, Sprinting, Uneven terrain running |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** SI joint responds best to symmetrical loading initially. Unilateral work should be loaded at 50% of bilateral capacity. Core stiffness (bracing, not movement) is the priority.

### Low Back Pain (Non-Specific Mechanical)

| Category | Safe (Green) | Modified (Yellow) | Contraindicated (Red) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Squat** | Goblet Squat (to 90°), Front Squat, Box Squat (to parallel) | Back Squat (low bar, moderate depth, belt), Hack Squat | Back Squat (heavy, full depth if painful), Good Morning |
| **Hinge** | Hip Thrust (bilateral), 45° Hyperextension (to parallel, not beyond), Trap Bar Deadlift (to knee) | Conventional Deadlift (light, to knee, belt) | Stiff-Leg Deadlift, Heavy conventional deadlift (full ROM), RDL (full ROM if painful) |
| **Core** | Dead bug, Side plank, Bird dog (McGill Big 3), Pallof press, Farmer's carry (bilateral) | Plank (30s holds, multiple sets), Suitcase carry (light) | Sit-up, Russian twist, Toes-to-bar, Hanging leg raise, Hyperextension (beyond neutral) |
| **Single Leg** | Step-Up (shallow, controlled), Reverse Lunge (short stride) | Bulgarian Split Squat (limited ROM, core braced) | Heavy lunge (deep), Single-leg deadlift (heavy) |
| **Cardio** | Walking (daily, start 20min), Cycling (upright position), Swimming | Elliptical (low resistance), Flat running (reduce mileage, softer surface) | Running on hard surfaces, Sprinting, Impact loading before core stability established |

**Modification notes for Yellow:** Movement exploration (find pain-relieving positions/ movements) is the first step. McGill Big 3 (curl-up, side plank, bird dog) should be performed daily. Spine must be kept in neutral position during ALL loaded exercises.
